subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & SDK integration next steps
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity & SDK integration next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Alex 1 really appreciate the deep dive. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your infra team aligned with our integration plan.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary goal: integrate Redwood inference into Acme's product for real-time assistants and semantic search (embeddings + reranker).
- Preferred deployment: private connectivity from Acme VPC to Redwood (reduce public egress, maintain data residency).
- Primary concerns: private DNS resolution, mTLS or IP allowlists, egress restrictions, and embedding storage routing.

Action items / questions for your network/security team
1) Connectivity: Can you accept AWS PrivateLink (Private Service Connect on GCP) or do you need an IP allowlist for outbound to our hosted endpoints? If IP allowlist, we need the set of source CIDRs.
2) DNS: Will you require a private hosted zone so the endpoint resolves internally (preferred), or do you want to use NAT + public endpoint?
3) Auth: Are you open to token-based API keys with mTLS client certs for mutual auth, or do you require IP-allowlisting-only for initial rollout?
4) Embeddings / vector DB: Will you host your vector DB in the same VPC (preferred) or should we push embeddings to a managed vector store?

What Redwood will provide
- SDK quickstart (attached) with examples for Java/Go/Python and recommended auth flows.
- Private connectivity guide and a short checklist for network teams (attached).
- A technical design session with Jonas (solutions) to walk through PrivateLink/PSC options and DNS configuration.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-integration-checklist.pdf, sdk-quickstart.zip (stubs).

Proposed next step: 45160 minute design call 1 here are times that work on our side: Wed 6/23 10:0011:00 PT or Thu 6/24 8:009:00 PT. Please loop in your security contact so we can address cert exchange and any questionnaire items.

Thanks 1 talk soon 

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa 1 thanks for the summary and clear action items. Looping in Sonia (security) on the thread as requested. Quick answers from our side: 

1) Connectivity: Our infra runs primarily in GCP but we also have some AWS accounts. Ideally we'd prefer a privately routed option (GCP Private Service Connect or AWS PrivateLink) to avoid public egress. If that's not feasible for an initial POC, we can do IP allowlisting for outbound to Redwood's public API. I'll confirm which route is quicker for our infra team.

2) DNS: We prefer private DNS so services in our VPC resolve the Redwood endpoint internally.

3) Auth: For production we require mTLS + token-based auth. For the POC we can accept token auth and an IP allowlist temporarily. 

4) Embeddings: We'll host the vector DB in our VPC (we use a managed vector store in GCP). Ideally the vector store will be in the same region as the Redwood private endpoint to reduce latencies.

I've attached a simple topology diagram (acme-network-topology.png) for context. Our security lead is Sonia Gupta (sonia.gupta@acme.com) 1 she'll handle the questionnaire and cert exchange process. 

We can do Wed 6/23 10:00 PT for the design session 1 that works for our network team.

Thanks,
Alex

Thanks Alex 1 great context. A few technical notes ahead of the design session so we can hit the ground running: 

- Supported private connectivity:
  * AWS: we support AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoint service).
  * GCP: Private Service Connect is supported (regional).
  * For hybrid clouds we can provision cross-cloud DNS records and provide a private ingress that peers via your networking preferences.

- DNS: We can provide a private hosted zone (overlay) that maps your internal DNS name (e.g., redwood-api.acme.internal) to the private endpoint IPs. That allows your services to resolve via internal DNS and avoids NAT.

- mTLS / cert exchange:
  * We support mutual TLS with client cert validation. Typical flow: you generate a CSR per environment and we sign/validate on our side, or we can support a short-lived cert exchange via an SFTP/secure form if your security team prefers.
  * We recommend token + mTLS for production (tokens for identity, mTLS for network-level auth).

- IP allowlist: If you need to start with an IP allowlist, we can provide a stable set of egress IP ranges. Note that ranges differ by region and may change with capacity; we can notify you for planned changes and support a small overlap window for rollouts.

- Embeddings / reranker routing:
  * If your vector DB lives in the same VPC, we can route embeddings writes over the private path so data never traverses public internet. 
  * If you use Redwood-managed embeddings, we'll push vectors to your chosen store using a private egress route or a VPC peering connection.

- Ports & DNS requirements: 443 (HTTPS) open for the private endpoint; if you rely on private DNS across accounts you may need port 53 (UDP/TCP) between resolvers, otherwise we can push conditional forwarders.

Pre-reqs for the design call:
- Network contact and security contact on the call (Sonia).
- Current topology diagram (thanks for that).
- List of source CIDRs if you want IP-allowlisting as a temporary fallback.

Attaching our private connectivity guide (rdw-vpc-private-connectivity-guide.pdf) and a short checklist. See you Wed 6/23 10:00 PT 1 I've tentatively added the meeting to our calendars.

Jonas Weber
